vt29_templars.topic: Templars: founding 1119/1120, Troyes 1129, Omne datum optimum 1139, finance, arrests 13 Oct 1307, Chinon 1308, Vienne 1312, Molay 1314; Friday-13 and Chinon-innocence errors corrected

claims.text: Hugh of Payns and Godfrey of Saint-Omer began the order in 1119 guarding pilgrims on the Jaffa-Jerusalem road; Baldwin II and Patriarch Warmund gave them a base on the Temple platform (al-Aqsa, 'Temple of Solomon'); church sanction probably at Nablus, January 1120; Troyes, January 1129, produced a Latin Rule of 71 clauses; Bernard of Clairvaux wrote In Praise of the New Knighthood
Omne datum optimum, Innocent II, 29 March 1139: privileges to master Robert of Craon; Templars 'defenders of the Catholic Church'; possessions under papal protection

Arrests in France in early hours of Friday 13 October 1307 by Philip IV's officials acting for papal inquisitors; charges: denial of Christ, spitting on the crucifix, indecent kissing, sodomy, idol worship; near-unanimous confessions in Oct-Nov 1307; 'Torture was freely used'; Clement V protested then issued Pastoralis praeeminentiae 22 November 1307 ordering all monarchs to arrest Templars

By early May 1310 almost 600 Templars had agreed to defend the order; 12 May 1310 fifty-four burnt outside Paris as relapsed heretics; Molay and Geoffroi de Charney sentenced 18 March 1314 and burnt that evening on the Ile des Javiaux

Chinon inquiry 17-20 August 1308 by cardinals Berenger Fredol, Etienne de Suisy, Landolfo Brancacci; records confessions, pleas for pardon and absolution from excommunication restoring the leaders to the sacraments; does not declare the Order innocent; Poitiers absolutions 2 July 1308; original D 217, authentic copy D 218; Frale found it September 2001, published J. Medieval History 30 (2004) 109-134; Processus contra Templarios 2007, 799 copies plus one for Benedict XVI; Baluze 1693 published a different Chinon parchment addressed to Philip IV

Vox in excelso, Vienne 22 March 1312, approved 3 April 1312: suppression 'not by definitive sentence, but by apostolic provision or ordinance'; reasons scandal and infamy 'impossible to allay as long as the order continues to exist'; entering or wearing the habit incurs automatic excommunication; more than four-fifths favoured suppression by provision
Ad providam, Vienne 2 May 1312: Templar property granted to the Hospital of St John; property in Castile, Aragon, Portugal and Majorca reserved to the apostolic see

Friday 13 superstition not from the Templar arrests; Lachenmeyer: before 20th c. 'Friday the 13th' not necessarily a concept; 1907 novel Friday, the Thirteenth; Da Vinci Code popularised the Templar link; Holy Blood, Holy Grail 1980s

Templars generated letters of credit for pilgrims who deposited valuables; Philip short of money for war with England; arrests released him from repaying large Templar loans; Philip kept much Templar property in France despite grant to Hospitallers; Order of Christ in Portugal
The Paris Temple soon became 'banker to kings'; the king's treasury accounts kept at the Temple 1221-1295

Audit: five leaders questioned at Chinon: Jacques de Molay, Raymbaud de Caron, Hugues de Pairaud, Geoffroi de Gonneville, Geoffroi de Charney; denials described as 'in words only, not in spirit'; Anne Gilmour-Bryson warns of the effect of torture on the answers; Baluze's 1693 document (Chinon, 20 Aug 1308) is the cardinals' letter to Philip IV reporting absolution of confessing Templars; the parchment shows the pope establishing the order was not heretical and capable of reform
Audit: Vox in excelso: 'legal process against the order up to now does not permit its canonical condemnation as heretical by definitive sentence'

vt29_bruno_galileo.topic: Bruno trial 1592-1600 and Yates thesis; Galileo 1616/1633 and 1979-1992 review

claims.text: Bruno b. Nola Feb 1548, Dominican, ordained 1572; infinite universe, stars as suns with planets; denounced by Mocenigo, arrested Venice 22 May 1592; sent to Rome Jan 1593; about seven years held; charges: denial of Trinity, deity of Christ, Incarnation, Mary's virginity, transubstantiation, plural worlds, metempsychosis, magic and divination; Bellarmine demanded full recantation; declared heretic 20 January 1600 by Clement VIII; Schopp reports 'Perhaps you pronounce this sentence against me with greater fear than I receive it'; burned Campo de' Fiori 17 February 1600, tongue restrained; works on Index 1603; statue 9 June 1889; Yates (Hermetic thesis) criticised by Gatti 2002; 2000 Sodano 'sad episode'
Sommario of the Bruno trial found 15 November 1940 by Angelo Mercati, published 1942; original trial volumes lost; late interrogation c. April 1599 on cosmology from La cena and De l'infinito
Bruno sentenced as an 'obstinate heretic'; denied the mercy of strangulation; 'dangerous interest' in high magic, Hermetic texts

Galileo: 24 Feb 1616 qualifiers: heliocentrism 'foolish and absurd in philosophy, and formally heretical'; 26 Feb Bellarmine's admonition (scope disputed); 5 Mar 1616 Index decree, De revolutionibus suspended until corrected, Foscarini banned; Dialogue 1632; 22 June 1633 'vehemently suspect of heresy', abjuration, imprisonment commuted to house arrest, Dialogue banned; Siena then Arcetri; 1758 general ban dropped; 1820 Settele; 1835 Index omits Copernicus and Dialogue; 1979 call, 1992 statement that theologians erred

Coyne: 10 Nov 1979 JPII call; 3 July 1981 commission (Garrone); 31 Oct 1992 Poupard report and papal address: 'tragic mutual incomprehension', 'a sort of myth'; the decision 'hasty and unhappy' attributed to 'certain persons'; 1616 decree and 1633 sentence never explicitly reformed; conclusions not submitted to commission members

AP 1 Nov 1992: John Paul II said theologians erred by treating the literal sense of Scripture as explaining the physical world; 'tragic mutual incomprehension'; Salvini: 'a recognition of errors and of guilt'

Audit: Coyne's chapter is no. 13 of Ernan McMullin (ed.), The Church and Galileo, University of Notre Dame Press, 2005; 'Galileo and the Church' (2004) is a different title cited inside the chapter (Fantoli), not the host volume

Audit: Bruno entered the Dominican order at 17; fled Naples on learning an indictment was being prepared; ashes thrown into the Tiber; John Paul II's 2000 general apology for 'the use of violence that some have committed in the service of truth'
Audit: Sommario found 15 Nov 1940 by the Prefect of the Vatican Archives, Angelo Mercati, 'after 15 years of unsuccessful investigation'

vt29_mystics.topic: Beguines and Porete (1310), Vienne decrees, Eckhart (In agro dominico 1329), Alumbrados (1525 edict), Molinos (Coelestis Pastor 1687)

claims.text: Porete: Beguine, b. c.1258 probably Hainaut; Mirror of Simple Souls (Old French, probably 1290s), dialogue of Love, Reason, Virtues and Soul; the Annihilated Soul gives up everything except God through Love; Bishop Gui de Collemedio of Cambrai had it burned at Valenciennes in her presence (between 1296 and 1306); arrested 1308, handed to inquisitor William of Paris; refused to speak or take the oath; 21 theologians judged 15 propositions heretical (1310); burned Place de Greve, Paris, 1 June 1310 as relapsed heretic; Guillaume de Nangis reports crowd moved to tears; Guiard de Cressonessart imprisoned; Ad nostrum (Vienne) cites extracts; book circulated anonymously, Guarnieri identified her 1946

Vienne decree on Beguines: they promise obedience to no one, renounce no possessions, profess no approved rule; some 'argue and preach on the holy Trinity and the divine essence'; way of life forbidden under automatic excommunication; exception for faithful women living in hospices in penance

Eckhart c.1260-c.1328, Dominican, Paris master; ground of the soul, birth of God in the soul, detachment, Godhead beyond God; 'The Eye with which I see God is the same Eye with which God sees me'; Cologne trial 1326 (Archbishop Henry of Virneburg); appealed to Avignon; died probably 28 January 1328; Dominicans sought rehabilitation 1990s; 1992 Vatican letter (revealed 2010): never condemned by name, only propositions

In agro dominico, Avignon, 27 March 1329: 26 articles plus 2; first fifteen and last two heretical, eleven 'evil-sounding' and 'very rash'; Eckhart died before the end and 'absolutely and totally revoked' the passages, submitting to papal judgment

Alumbrados: first leaders Isabel de la Cruz and Pedro Ruiz de Alcaraz; held soul could reach perfection, sacraments superfluous, sin impossible in union; Inquisitor General Alonso Manrique's 1525 edict listed 48 propositions; Ignatius of Loyola examined at Salamanca 1527, admonished; generally not executed; 1529 Toledo group whipped and imprisoned; Molinos accused of resembling them

Dejamiento: passive abandonment to God's love vs recogimiento (Osuna); Alcaraz: 'El amor de Dios en un hombre es Dios'; 1525 edict prop. 11 (leaving all to God suffices, fasting and works of mercy unnecessary); Maria de Cazalla detained 22 April 1532, after two years and torture abjured de levi, fined 100 ducats; compared to Porete's Mirror

Molinos: Spiritual Guide Rome 1675, Madrid 1676, twenty editions in twelve years; 'interior annihilation'; c.12,000 letters found; 3 Sept 1687 sentence read at Santa Maria sopra Minerva: 'dogmatic heretic', life imprisonment; moral charges alleged; died Rome 28 December 1696

Molinos arrested 18 July 1685; Segneri's 1680 Concordia; abjured 3 Sept 1687; Coelestis Pastor 20 November 1687 condemned 68 propositions (annihilation of the soul's powers, cessation of acts, indifference to salvation, uselessness of resisting temptation); 'prayer of quiet'
Britannica: Molinos taught people must 'banish their individual wills'; condemned doctrines do not appear in the Guide; reversal attributed to discovered immorality held in Vatican files
Luis de Leon imprisoned by Inquisition at Valladolid 27 March 1572-Dec 1576, cleared 11 Dec 1576; published first collected edition of Teresa of Avila's works 1588

Audit: Denzinger heading: Molinos's errors 'Condemned in the decree of the Sacred Office, August 28, and in the Constitutions "Coelestis Pastor," Nov. 20, 1687'. Variant dates: Catholic Encyclopedia 'Molinos' gives 2 November 1687, its 'Innocent XI' article 19 November 1687; Denzinger's 20 November is used
Audit: Porete quoted 'I am God, says Love, for Love is God and God is Love'; Mirror translated after her death into Latin, Italian and Middle English; at one point thought to be by John of Ruusbroec

Audit: Catholic Encyclopedia: the Guide was 'approved by various theologians and by ecclesiastical authority'; moral charges: Molinos claimed acts committed by himself were not blameworthy as free will had no part in them
